observations: Photo shows an indoor split-unit AC head sitting on top of its matching outdoor condenser unit, both placed on an outdoor tiled floor near a wooden door.
Indoor unit front panel has a small printed rating/label area but the text is too small and low-resolution to read any brand, model or BTU/HP rating.
Outdoor condenser has a hand-written pink/red marker mark that appears to read '...nverter' - this looks like a seller-applied label, not a manufacturer plate.
Dust and some discoloration visible on both units, consistent with outdoor storage or disuse.
No power cable, remote control, compressor nameplate, or refrigerant pipes clearly visible in the frame.
No visible physical damage (no dents, cracks) but image resolution and angle do not allow close inspection of the fan blades, coils, or rear pipe connections.

claims.evidence: Photo 0 shows no way to test power-on, cooling, or compressor function; 'faulty' is seller's own description and cannot be confirmed or denied remotely.
Photo 0 shows a hand-written mark resembling 'inverter' on the outdoor unit, but this is not a manufacturer plate or stamped spec, so it is unconfirmed.
No photo evidence can confirm seller's stated location.

risks.risk: Unknown capacity/tonnage (e.g. 1HP vs 1.5HP vs 2HP), which strongly affects value
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the nameplate/rating label on indoor or outdoor unit showing BTU/HP and model number
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest common capacity tier for a faulty split AC

risks.risk: Extent of fault unknown (no cooling, compressor dead, just needs gas top-up, electrical fault, or stripped for parts)
risks.proof: A power-on test video showing it plugged in with any sound, fan movement, or error light, plus seller statement on what exactly is faulty

risks.risk: Missing or cut copper pipes/coils at the back of the outdoor unit (common when AC units are sold as 'faulty' after copper theft)
risks.proof: Photo of the rear of the outdoor unit showing intact piping and valves
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming pipes may be missing/cut, i.e. scrap/parts-only value

risks.risk: Missing accessories (remote control, power cable, mounting brackets)
risks.proof: Photo showing remote, cable, and brackets alongside the unit

risks.risk: Corrosion or compressor seizure not visible in this single angled photo
risks.proof: Close-up photos of compressor housing and coils from multiple angles
risks.if_unproven: priced as possible internal corrosion/seizure, i.e. worst case

proof_requests: Close-up, well-lit photo of the nameplate/rating label on both indoor and outdoor units (for brand, model, BTU/HP).
A short video of the unit being powered on, showing any response (fan spin, light, sound).
Photo of the rear of the outdoor unit showing the condition of copper pipes and valves.
Photo of included accessories (remote, cable, brackets) if any.
response.reason: The item is clearly a split-unit AC sold as faulty, but without a readable capacity/model label or any proof of the fault's extent and pipe/accessory condition, even a worst-case price cannot be reliably set.
